chapter_seo_title: Dao-Twisted World Ch. 231 — Li Huowang Hunts a Deadly Cure Beneath Qingqiu
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang finds Black Tai Sui skin and pursues its source, but Sun Baolu reveals a terrifying secret: Qingqiu's demons hide underground. Walking into the nest may be the only way forward.
og_description: A desperate hunt for a temporary cure leads Li Huowang to a forbidden hole in the earth—where the ground is a nest.
twitter_title: The Cure Is a Trap — Ch. 231
twitter_description: Li Huowang chases a scrap of dried skin into a forbidden tunnel. Sun Baolu begs him to stop. He doesn't.

lore_anchors.definition: A grotesque parasitic entity produced by twisted alchemical practices; its dried skin is believed by Li Huowang to temporarily block his hallucinations, though it dissolves into black water upon death.
A rare human constitution that makes the bearer a living alchemical ingredient; Li Huowang's condition is incurable, and his "hysteria" is the visible symptom of his identity instability.
The vast grassland region Li Huowang's group is traveling through; its lack of surface monsters is revealed to be a deception—the evil spirits are hiding in tunnels beneath the grass.
A term for a mental breakdown involving dissociative or psychosomatic symptoms; in this novel's context, it describes the visible, public collapse of Li Huowang's cognitive stability.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang trust a dry scrap of skin?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He tasted it and recognized the unique texture from his past experience with Black Tai Sui. In the Dao-Twisted World, sensory memory is often the only reliable anchor he has left.

Qingqiu's green grass covers a hidden underground ecosystem of supernatural entities. The Great Khan prohibits even discussion of it, because thinking about or naming the things below can attract them.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Black Tai Sui a permanent cure?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Li Huowang believes it can block his hallucinations temporarily. Its flesh dissolves on death, and the solution it offers is described as "a rotting bandage"—a short-term patch on an incurable wound.
